purpose: Goal cap fixture: a direct human turn creates a goal with max_goal_rounds=1; the driver runs round 1, then blocks the goal with code round-limit instead of queueing round 2, so no further turn starts.

dshSource.note: Constructed from the round-limit branch: at maxGoalRounds the driver blocks with code round-limit and message "Goal reached its configured limit of N rounds."

tokens.note: Recorded workspace path; the fixture host substitutes its temp workspace.
System prompt text token; the prompt is pinned by the P1 plain-turn fixture.
Whole tool-schema array token; the nine schemas are pinned by the P1 fixtures.
Goal command identity; generated as goal-cmd-1 by the fixture host.

fixtureOrdinalTokens.note: Ordinal message identity bound to msg-1.
Ordinal message identity bound to system-1.
Ordinal message identity bound to assistant-1-1.
Ordinal message identity bound to msg-2.
Ordinal message identity bound to assistant-1-2.
Ordinal message identity bound to goal-round-goal-1-1-1.
Ordinal message identity bound to assistant-2-1.

volatile.note: Pinned deterministic goal clock (fixture host now_ms=300); real recordings use wall time.

openIssues: Constructed scenario: the only live goal recording has maxGoalRounds=256 and never reaches the cap. The expected log is bound to the native cap branch.
The create_goal tool path is used because /goal create does not accept a cap.
